title: Bounded execution of a while loop
statement: Let $L$ be a resource limit with word bound $w\in\mathbb Z$, space bound $s\in\mathbb N$, and depth bound $h\in\mathbb N$; let $P$ be a finite program, $d,n,T\in\mathbb N$, and let $\sigma$ be an initial state, $c$ a loop condition, $b$ a body statement, $Q$ a predicate on states, and $I_j$ a state predicate for each $j\in\mathbb N$. Suppose $I_0(\sigma)$ holds, and for every $j<n$ and state $\tau$ with $I_j(\tau)$, the condition $c$ is safe at $\tau$ and true there, while $b$ is block-safe at $\tau$ and its resulting state satisfies $I_{j+1}$. Suppose also that for every state $\tau$ satisfying $I_n(\tau)$, $c$ is safe at $\tau$ and false there, and $Q(\tau)$ holds. If $n\bigl(\operatorname{cost}(c)+1+\operatorname{blockCost}(b)\bigr)+\operatorname{cost}(c)+1\le T$, then executing the loop with condition $c$ and body $b$ from $\sigma$, under limits $L$, program $P$, and depth parameter $d$, ends in some state satisfying $Q$ with execution cost at most $T$.
